question: A Canadian household includes a 27-year-old adult, their mother and their grandmother, all living together. Why is this classified as multigenerational rather than just a parent living with an adult child in Statistics Canada's 2021 Census studies?
generated_answer: The 2021 Census of Population defines a household as a person or a group of persons who occupy the same dwelling and do not have a usual place of residence elsewhere in Canada. The definition of a household is based on the dwelling and not on the family relationships of the household members. The 2021 Census of Population provides information on the characteristics of the household members, including their age, sex, and relationship to the person who is the first person listed on the questionnaire. The relationship to the person who is the first person listed on the questionnaire is based on the family relationships of the household members. In the example provided, the 27-year-old adult, their mother, and their grandmother are all living together in the same dwelling and do not have a usual place of residence elsewhere in Canada. Therefore, they are classified as a household. The 2021 Census of Population does not provide information on the family relationships of the household members beyond the relationship to the person who is the first person listed on the questionnaire. Therefore, it is not possible to determine whether the household is multigenerational or not based on the information provided in the 2021 Census of Population.
